parties.selection: Leader Qiulae Wong and deputy leader Daniel Eb (list places 1 and 2). As a party outside Parliament it gets a shorter profile.
parties.history: Founded in 2016 by economist Gareth Morgan as The Opportunities Party (TOP). It has never won a seat (2.22% in 2023). Qiulae Wong became leader in November 2025 and the party rebranded as The Opportunity Party.
parties.ideology: Self-described centrist, 'evidence-based' and radical centrist. Wong says supporters are 'politically homeless'. A Talbot Mills analysis found about a third of its supporters came from the left and a third from the right (secondary source).
parties.role: Outside Parliament. The 13 October 1News–Verian poll put it on 8% (about 10 seats), the clearest kingmaker position in recent polling; the final Post/Freshwater Strategy poll (20 October) had it on 5.4%, just over the threshold. Luxon has again ruled out working with it; ACT's David Seymour said on 15 October he would be open to a bloc including it. Wong says Opportunity will speak first to the largest party by seats on election night, and won't support a government with Winston Peters as foreign minister.
policies: Five post-election bottom lines: a stronger Commerce Commission; lobbying regulation and donation caps; a 10-year health plan; phasing out bottom trawling; and recommitting to the Paris Agreement with an independent Climate Change Commission.
https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/1643401/health-supermarkets-and-political-lobbying-among-opportunity-party-s-bottom-lines
A land value tax (not one of the bottom lines), citizens' assemblies, and a methane ETS (secondary source).
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opportunity_Party_(New_Zealand)
events: Luxon ruled out Opportunity in July 2026 and reaffirmed this at the 6 October debate. Wong says she does not believe him.
https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/1809836/opportunity-leader-qiulae-wong-doesn-t-believe-luxon-rule-out
Peters called the party's candidates 'communists' and its bottom lines a 'wrinkly derrière'. Shane Jones called its policies 'not rational'.
https://newsroom.co.nz/2026/09/11/parties-rule-out-deals-to-get-opportunitys-qiulae-wong-over-the-line-in-heartland-seat/

13 October 2026: Qiulae Wong took part in TVNZ's Multi-Party Debate. She said Opportunity would negotiate first with the largest party and told the Greens they could have stopped 'egregious' coalition moves by working with National.
https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/10/13/you-poor-thing-six-big-moments-from-the-multi-party-debate/

15 October 2026: ACT's David Seymour said a coalition including Opportunity to keep a left-wing government out 'would be a good outcome', while doubting Opportunity would be the kingmaker. National has ruled Opportunity out on multiple occasions.
https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/1932454/four-headed-beast-act-leader-david-seymour-hints-at-potential-for-coalition-with-opportunity

19 October 2026: Luxon again said he would not work with Opportunity and that ACT could go with Opportunity 'outside of government' if it wished. He warned against strategic voting: 'I'm not sure you always know what you're going to get with a minor party.'
https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/2010803/as-it-happened-election-campaign-19-october
14 October 2026, ASB finance debate: Wong joined Edmonds, Jones and Swarbrick in backing a bed tax for Queenstown, and backed a cross-party review of superannuation.
https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/1905390/what-we-learnt-from-a-rough-and-tumble-finance-debate

people.name: Christopher Luxon
people.role: Prime Minister; Leader of the National Party; Minister for National Security and Intelligence
people.seat: MP for Botany (since 2020); contesting Botany
people.background: Former chief executive of Air New Zealand and a former Unilever executive. Entered Parliament in 2020, became National leader in November 2021 and Prime Minister in November 2023.
positions: 'No new taxes' (no bank tax, no bed tax); tough welfare obligations, including drug testing for Jobseekers.
Has ruled out working with the Opportunity Party because of its land value tax; calls vote-splitting 'insanely stupid'.
Campaigns on economic 'turnaround' and 'fixing the basics'.
reversals: National's tax pledge was originally 'no new taxes on working people'. In August 2026 Luxon widened it to 'no new taxes', dropping a bank tax and bed tax that ministers (including Willis) had floated earlier in the year.

In early May 2026 Luxon said National would 'go to the election with another election policy around superannuation and lifting the retirement age for sure'. Its 12 October fiscal plan set no date for raising the age and committed to cross-party talks instead. National says its stance has not changed.

quotes.text: The least someone can do is go get registered and enrolled to vote 12 days out from election day. It's not rocket science.
quotes.context: Told NewstalkZB, laughing off opposition claims of voter suppression over the end of same-day and advance-voting enrolment (RNZ live blog).

quotes.text: I announced very clearly to you back then when the election date would be, and yeah, there's a number of dates it could be. We picked this date. It's as simple as that.
quotes.context: Responding to RNZ's report that the Electoral Commission had called 7 November 'challenging, but manageable' and favoured other dates.

quotes.text: It was stuck for years and years. National’s fast-track got it approved in five months. That’s clean, local power for around 12,000 homes.
quotes.context: X post from Westpower in Greymouth about the Waitaha hydro scheme.

quotes.text: No, I've ruled them out.
quotes.context: NZ Herald (NZME) leaders' debate with Chris Hipkins, 14 Oct evening, as reported in RNZ's analysis. Asked again whether he would call Opportunity's Qiulae Wong if he needed her party's support to form a government.

quotes.text: Chris Hipkins is the solution to the problems that Chris Hipkins created
quotes.context: Reacting to the same 1News–Verian poll; 1News reported he said New Zealanders did not think this.

quotes.text: He can't find a pathway to get into government without those four radical parties and six leaders, that's going to be chaos.
quotes.context: On Chris Hipkins' likely coalition partners (Greens, Te Pāti Māori, Opportunity), RNZ Morning Report.

quotes.text: Chris Penk launched a leadership challenge this week, which resulted in today's confidence vote. This makes his role untenable, and as such I have removed his portfolios.
quotes.context: Statement removing Chris Penk's ministerial portfolios.

quotes.text: We've been doing a big turnaround, we've been fixing a lot of the basics. We now have an opportunity, as this recovery comes through, not just to watch it come through but to actually shape the future of this country...
quotes.context: Election-date announcement; pitching National's economic record.

people.name: Nicola Willis
people.role: Deputy Leader of the National Party; Minister of Finance; Minister for Economic Growth; Minister for Social Investment
people.seat: List MP; list rank 2 (not contesting an electorate)
people.background: Entered Parliament on the list in 2018 after a career as a political adviser and corporate lobbyist. Deputy leader since December 2021; Finance Minister since 2023; delivered Budget 2026 on 28 May.
positions: Fiscal restraint in an election year. Calls Labour's fiscal plan 'the least credible… in living memory'.
Personally favours raising the NZ Super age gradually. National's 2026 policy is cross-party talks within 100 days rather than a set date.

Tax relief only once the books are back in surplus (not forecast before 2029). On 14 October she signalled interest in future business tax relief (including the R&D tax credit and, over time, the corporate rate) alongside personal tax cuts when conditions allow.
Floated taxing banks 'fairly' in May 2026, then dropped it under the 'no new taxes' pledge.
reversals: In May 2026 she said 'We've got to make sure the banks are taxed fairly…'. On 23 August 2026 she explained why National would not pursue a bank tax.

quotes.text: The priorities for tax reform are more money in the back pockets of workers and then ensuring that our tax system encourages businesses to innovate, to be productive, and to make investments.
quotes.context: Ahead of the ASB finance spokesperson debate in Queenstown, signalling interest in future business tax relief once books allow.

quotes.text: New Zealand’s lack of a capital gains tax is a real competitive advantage over Australia, and we should embrace that by not introducing one.
quotes.context: National release announcing five first-100-days commitments aimed at keeping young New Zealanders at home or bringing them back.

quotes.text: While our fiscal plan shows a pathway to potential tax relief for working New Zealanders, now is not the time to cut taxes.
quotes.context: Releasing National's fiscal plan with Christopher Luxon

quotes.text: This is the least credible fiscal plan released by a major party in living memory.
quotes.context: National press release titled 'Labour's fiscal plan a fraud'. Labour says its plan is fully costed and funded.

quotes.text: It's a Budget that does what's right for the country... this is not a time to be getting us further into the hock, to be whacking another set of bills on the credit card.
quotes.context: RNZ Morning Report, asked whether a restrained Budget was risky in election year.

quotes.text: New Zealand is digging its way out of the post-Covid hole.
quotes.context: Delivering Budget 2026.

quotes.text: Kiwis can look forward with confidence, they just need to choose it, they just need to vote for it.
quotes.context: Closing line of her Budget 2026 speech.

quotes.text: One for all, all for one. And when the caucus, by majority, have confidence in the leader, then we all stand together, backing the leader.
quotes.context: As deputy leader, after Luxon survived the April caucus confidence vote.

people.name: Chris Bishop
people.role: Attorney-General (since April 2026); Minister of Housing; Infrastructure; Transport; RMA Reform
people.seat: MP for Hutt South; contesting Hutt South
people.background: First entered Parliament as a list MP in 2014. Leader of the House until April 2026, and campaign chair until the April reshuffle, when he became Attorney-General. Led the RMA replacement and the first National Infrastructure Plan.
positions: Planning reform: says the new system should make fast-track unnecessary within five years.
Backed Luxon in the April confidence vote, describing the caucus discussion as 'good, honest and robust'.

quotes.text: If re-elected, National will get it under construction early next year.
quotes.context: National release 'Backing Waikato', on the SH1 Cambridge to Piarere extension of the Waikato Expressway.

quotes.text: The blanket ban on minimum car parking requirements has not worked. The economic theory behind it did not account for the reality of New Zealand's suburban streets.
quotes.context: Launching National's Auckland plan as transport spokesperson.

quotes.text: They've literally released a press release that says they will change the law to do things that are already in the law.
quotes.context: On coalition partner NZ First's fast-track housing policy.

quotes.text: I will consider the reforms to have failed.
quotes.context: Newsroom interview: if, in five years, the new planning system has not made the fast-track regime unnecessary.

quotes.text: Today is a major milestone. After 35 years of the RMA, Parliament has passed legislation for a fundamentally different way of planning for New Zealand's future.
quotes.context: Press release as the Planning Bill and Natural Environment Bill (RMA replacement) passed third reading.

quotes.text: Passing these Bills is not the end of the job. The next task is making sure the new system works in practice.
quotes.context: Same release; the full new system is intended to operate by 2030.

quotes.text: I think what the Prime Minister was saying, which I would broadly agree with, is that the country has very difficult challenges ahead of it and we should spend our time focused on those challenges.
quotes.context: After voting in support of Luxon in the April caucus confidence vote; he described the caucus discussion as "good, honest and robust".

quotes.text: Obviously I love being the campaign chair, and it's a role I enjoy doing, but it's fine - I've got plenty of things to do.
quotes.context: After losing the campaign-chair and Leader of the House roles in the April reshuffle while becoming Attorney-General.

people.name: Simeon Brown
people.role: Minister of Health; Minister for Energy; State Owned Enterprises; National campaign chair (since April 2026)
people.seat: MP for Pakuranga (since 2017); contesting Pakuranga
people.background: Elected in 2017. Minister of Energy, Transport and Local Government from 2023. Moved to Health in January 2025. Regained Energy and became campaign chair in the April 2026 reshuffle.
positions: Campaigns hard against Labour's record and its capital gains tax (including the ASA-reviewed ad).
As Health Minister, paused new puberty-blocker prescriptions for gender dysphoria in November 2025, pending a UK trial.

quotes.text: And it also highlights where further work and further investment is needed to make sure that we are seeing improvements across the country.
quotes.context: Told RNZ, on emergency department figures showing a national improvement but about half of hospitals going backwards (published 17 Oct; interview date not stated).

quotes.text: Making your own power should be as easy as plugging in a toaster.
quotes.context: As National's energy spokesperson, announcing that shops would be able to sell plug-in solar panels within six months of a re-elected National government.

quotes.text: The claim is false. No child has had their cancer care suspended, and no child has missed out on care.
quotes.context: As Health Minister, responding to reports that nursing shortages had suspended some cancer treatment at Starship children's hospital. A mother told RNZ her toddler's treatment had been delayed.

quotes.text: The Advertising Standards Authority has not said KiwiSaver wouldn't be affected by Labour's capital gains tax - it has only suggested that KiwiSaver may not be impacted to the same extent as rental properties, baches and businesses.
quotes.context: Responding after the ASA partly upheld a complaint that a National attack ad on Labour's CGT was misleading.

quotes.text: Kiwis remember what life was like under Labour – inflation peaking, crime soaring, and public services like health and education going backwards.
quotes.context: LinkedIn post on becoming campaign chair.

quotes.text: I'm focused on making sure that we win in November and making sure that we deliver a National-led government.
quotes.context: On taking over as campaign chair; asked his experience, he replied "winning elections".

quotes.text: I have never been part of a conversation where that has been said to our prime minister.
quotes.context: Asked repeatedly whether he had been in a conversation telling Luxon he was losing caucus support.

quotes.text: These changes are about ensuring treatments are safe and carefully managed, while maintaining access to care for those who need it.
quotes.context: As Health Minister, announcing a pause on new puberty-blocker prescriptions for gender dysphoria pending a UK trial.

people.name: Erica Stanford
people.role: Minister of Education; Minister of Immigration; lead minister on the Royal Commission (abuse in care) response
people.seat: MP for East Coast Bays (since 2017); contesting East Coast Bays
people.background: Elected in 2017. Leads the replacement of NCEA and the school curriculum changes. Widely named in media as a possible alternative leader during the August 2026 challenge, which she denied any part in.
positions: Replacing NCEA with new qualifications ('clear, rigorous and widely understood').
Says she did not challenge for, or count numbers for, the leadership.
people.note: Labour's Willie Jackson publicly said 'Nobody believes her' about her denial. That is his claim; it is recorded on his profile.

quotes.text: There is no time to waste when around 60,000 children start school every year. The work is not finished, but the early signs show why this government has been so relentlessly focused on evidence, implementation and getting support into classrooms quickly.
quotes.context: Told RNZ for its analysis of the government's education changes this term (curriculum rewrite, NCEA replacement). Labour would freeze the NCEA reforms.

quotes.text: Labour is asking New Zealanders to put them back in charge of education, but they can’t even agree among themselves what their education policy is.
quotes.context: National release after Hipkins said at the NZ Herald leaders' debate that the hour-a-day reading, writing and maths requirement should be left to schools, and Edmonds earlier said Labour would not change it.

quotes.text: There is still a long way to go, but the evidence is mounting that we are turning things around. We cannot afford to go backwards.
quotes.context: As Education Minister, on new NZCER Progressive Achievement Test results showing gains in maths and reading for primary and intermediate students (National release).

quotes.text: I didn't challenge for the leadership.
quotes.context: First media appearance after the failed Penk leadership challenge, amid speculation she was the alternative leader.

quotes.text: I want to be the minister of Education and Immigration - mostly education - for the next nine years. I love my job, and I've got so much more to do.
quotes.context: Same appearance, ruling herself out of leadership ambitions.

quotes.text: I didn't do any numbers at all. I can categorically tell you, I don't know if anyone did do any numbers. I certainly didn't.
quotes.context: Denying she counted caucus votes for Chris Penk's challenge.

quotes.text: This qualification rewards hard work and is designed to encourage young people to strive to do their very best, and ultimately to feel proud of what they achieved.
quotes.context: Confirming details of the qualification replacing NCEA (NZCE at Year 12, NZACE at Year 13).

quotes.text: We want young people leaving school with qualifications that are clear, rigorous and widely understood by parents, employers, tertiary providers and students themselves.
quotes.context: National Party release on the NCEA replacement.

people.name: Chris Hipkins
people.role: Leader of the Labour Party; Leader of the Opposition
people.seat: MP for Remutaka (since 2008); contesting Remutaka
people.background: Was Education Minister and Covid-19 Response Minister in the Ardern government, and Prime Minister from January to November 2023. Has led Labour since January 2023.
positions: Election framed as being 'about the cost of living'.
A property-only capital gains tax to fund three free GP visits a year; a 10% student-loan write-off.
Says talks with Opportunity are 'conversations to be had after the election'.
reversals: In July 2023 he said: "under a government I lead there will be no wealth or capital gains tax after the election. End of story." In October 2025 Labour adopted a 28% CGT on property. After the 2023 loss he put tax options back on the table, and he says the CGT is narrow and targeted.
RNZ background on the 2025 decision and earlier ruling-out.

quotes.text: Christopher Luxon doesn't want to talk about it, but everyone else does. So today, I'm challenging Christopher Luxon: come and debate me on health.
quotes.context: In a social media video challenging Luxon to a debate on health, after Luxon denied the health system was in crisis (RNZ).

quotes.text: The key thing we'd want to look at there is making sure that we're not doing anything that makes things worse for younger employees. And right at the moment, youth unemployment is a major issue. I want to leave no stone unturned in getting young people into jobs.
quotes.context: Asked in Auckland about the Greens' plan to abolish the training wage; he said Labour had not looked at it and wanted to review the evidence on employment effects.

quotes.text: I think it was really, really ill considered, they made a real error of judgement here.
quotes.context: Speaking in Rotorua about Green and Te Pāti Māori candidates posing for photos at a Mongrel Mob election hui. He also said any of his potential ministers who did so 'wouldn't be a member of the cabinet'.

quotes.text: [National] think women should settle for being paid less than men. I don't.
quotes.context: NZ Herald (NZME) leaders' debate with Chris Hipkins, 14 Oct evening, as reported in RNZ's analysis. Defending care and support workers after Luxon said Labour had not funded its pay equity promise. Bracketed word is RNZ's.

quotes.text: We've got some real on-the-ground momentum everywhere we go ... People are raising the same issues with us. The cost of living is out of control. The current government's doing nothing about it. We can't afford three more years of this government.
quotes.context: Same poll reaction interview.

quotes.text: This election is about the cost of living. This election is about your cost of living.
quotes.context: Opening of his campaign launch speech in Manukau.

quotes.text: Backstabbing and infighting just means more delay and more distraction for New Zealand. If National can't govern itself, how can New Zealanders trust it to govern the country?
quotes.context: Media release after Luxon survived the Penk leadership challenge.

quotes.text: #BREAKING: Labour will provide three free doctor's visits a year for everyone, delivered via a brand new Medicard and funded by a targeted tax on property profits, excluding the family home.
quotes.context: X post announcing Labour's flagship health/tax policy.

people.name: Carmel Sepuloni
people.role: Deputy Leader of the Labour Party
people.seat: Electorate MP (Kelston); contesting the new Glendene electorate
people.background: List MP 2008–11, MP for Kelston since 2014. Social Development Minister throughout the Ardern government, Deputy Prime Minister in 2023, and Labour deputy leader since 2023. First MP of Tongan descent.
positions: Visa-waiver travel for Pacific Islands Forum citizens, while 'the rules still apply' on overstaying.
Opposed the move-on orders bill as 'purely ideological'.

quotes.text: We're talking about seamless travel between Pacific countries and New Zealand … and a recognition of the cost and burden that the current system puts on New Zealand Pacific families.
quotes.context: Announcing Labour's pledge to extend visa-waiver travel to Pacific Islands Forum citizens.

quotes.text: Our relationship has matured enough for us to be able to move to a place that they have access to the same electronic system that 60 other countries have. It's the right thing to do.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: The expectation is that the rules still apply … and our expectation is that people will follow them.
quotes.context: Responding to concerns about rising overstayer rates.

quotes.text: It's not nice, and it's hard when you have to explain it to your kids, but it's even worse for the people that are actually living as homeless people, because they have nowhere to lay down with a roof over their heads at night time.
quotes.context: First-reading debate on the move-on orders bill, which she called "purely ideological".

people.name: Barbara Edmonds
people.role: Finance spokesperson
people.seat: Electorate MP (Mana); contesting the new Kenepuru electorate
people.background: MP for Mana since 2020. Minister of Revenue, Internal Affairs and Pacific Peoples in the final year of the Labour government (2023). Now Labour's finance spokesperson.
positions: Defends the CGT revenue assumptions (about 3% house-price growth) as 'conservative'.
Says income-tax cuts should come 'as the fiscal and economic environment allows'.

quotes.text: It's around supporting them to make things easier for them to run their business, so they get paid on time and to make sure that they get a bigger cut of government business, because the government procures about $50 billion worth of goods and services.
quotes.context: On Labour's small-business focus, ahead of the ASB finance spokesperson debate.

quotes.text: Not Chlöe Swarbrick and not Nicola Willis - Barbara Edmonds the MP for Kenepuru will be.
quotes.context: ASB finance debate in Queenstown, 14 Oct evening, as reported by RNZ. Opening remarks, on who would be the next finance minister.

quotes.text: I don't have to copy Nicola, we are two very different people.
quotes.context: ASB finance debate in Queenstown, 14 Oct evening, as reported by RNZ. Asked what businesses that use Investment Boost would do if Labour scrapped it.

quotes.text: Three years on from National's promise to get things moving, 171,000 Kiwis are out of work, business liquidations are at a 15-year high, and 2000 people are leaving the country every week. National had its chance, and families are worse off for it.
quotes.context: Launching Labour's economic plan (venture capital, small-business and apprenticeship measures).

quotes.text: You need to have the strong mandate to do it. They wanted the mandate to do it, they could have put it in their policy ... that conversation still continues, even if they're in government, [or] we're in government.
quotes.context: Responding to National's superannuation stance; Labour would keep the age at 65 (reported by RNZ)

quotes.text: We get about 3.1% on average over the forecast period. So we believe the 3% is conservative, and we think is prudent given that the forecasts do change...
quotes.context: interest.co.nz interview defending the house-price growth assumption behind Labour's CGT revenue.

quotes.text: I don't want it going heaps over or heaps under. For me, [it] is just making sure there is... steady and stable house prices.
quotes.context: Same interview, asked what Labour wants for house prices.

quotes.text: Tax cuts need to be allowed as the fiscal and economic environment allows for it.
quotes.context: Same interview, on whether income-tax changes are possible once in surplus.

people.name: Willie Jackson
people.role: Senior MP; Māori development spokesperson (as reported)
people.seat: List MP; list rank 4 (not contesting an electorate)
people.background: Former unionist, broadcaster and urban Māori leader. Alliance MP 1999–2002 and Labour MP since 2017. Minister for Māori Development in the Labour government. Leads Labour's campaign for the Māori electorates.
positions: Critical of Te Pāti Māori's overhang and candidate-vote strategy.
Concedes that unseating Māori-seat incumbents is hard.

quotes.text: You do not hand the government something, who are absolutely desperate at the moment, desperate, and then all of a sudden you go and have a campaign meeting with the, come on, with the Mob
quotes.context: RNZ Morning Report, as Labour's Māori electorate campaign chair, saying the Mongrel Mob hui was not a good strategic move by Green and Te Pāti Māori candidates.

quotes.text: Chippy's not saying we're not going to support those families, of course we are. But we want to win an election here.
quotes.context: Same interview. He said Labour and Hipkins 'abhor' gangs but Labour would not walk away from supporting whānau in gangs.

quotes.text: We've got Māori youth unemployment at a record high. I think it's between 15 and 24. We're up around 25 percent.
quotes.context: Mata with Mihingarangi Forbes discussion with Paul Goldsmith; Jackson also called Crown–Māori relations an all-time low. Published 14 Oct; recording date not given.

quotes.text: I'm not a fool in terms of how hard it is to knock out incumbents.
quotes.context: RNZ interview on Labour's chances of winning all seven Māori electorates.

quotes.text: We weren't talking about voting for an overhang. We weren't talking about voting for people who had different politics from us, all we were talking about was using the system to get more Māori through Labour into the Parliament.
quotes.context: Responding to Debbie Ngarewa-Packer's charge that Labour used a similar strategy in 2017.

quotes.text: You can buy into that strategy if every everything's working well, but they're not even voting for themselves.
quotes.context: Criticising Te Pāti Māori's electorate-vote-only strategy, which he warned could invite a backlash against the Māori seats.

quotes.text: Nobody believes her. No one who is aware of the situation, who followed the situation, believes her.
quotes.context: On Erica Stanford's denial of involvement in the National leadership challenge.

people.name: Megan Woods
people.role: Senior MP; energy spokesperson (per 2026 releases)
people.seat: List-only in 2026; list rank 5 (formerly MP for Wigram)
people.background: MP for Wigram from 2011. A Cabinet minister in the 2017–23 Labour government (including Energy and Housing). List-only in 2026.
positions: Pro-renewables: SolarSaver subsidies and loans; would legalise plug-in solar for renters.

quotes.text: There's nothing complicated about these costings.
quotes.context: Launching Labour's $160m SolarSaver policy; asked if confident in the costings she said "we have our numbers right".

quotes.text: We don't have enough of the plug-in systems because they're illegal in New Zealand at the moment - the first step is making them legal.
quotes.context: Same launch, on plug-in solar for renters.

quotes.text: Solar is the future and an important part of our energy security, so anything that makes it easier and cheaper to install is welcome.
quotes.context: Labour release responding to National's home-energy loans policy.

quotes.text: Labour has and will always back renewable energy while National has spent three years making New Zealand's energy problems worse.
quotes.context: Same release.

people.name: Marama Davidson
people.role: Green Party co-leader
people.seat: List MP; list rank 1 (not contesting an electorate)
people.background: List MP since 2015 and co-leader since 2018. Minister for the Prevention of Family and Sexual Violence in 2020–23.
positions: Frames the Middle East conflict as 'a human catastrophe'; supports a rules-based international order.
Supports taxing wealth to fund essential services. Would revoke fast-track mining consents.

quotes.text: Oriini Kaipara made those comments, not the Green Party, and that is for Te Pāti Māori to answer to.
quotes.context: Asked whether the Greens also wanted to 'restore mana' to the Mongrel Mob (RNZ).

quotes.text: If we want people to enter trades and complete apprenticeships, it's time we fairly recognise their hard work instead of punishing them for trying to contribute.
quotes.context: Same announcement, at a building site in Auckland.

quotes.text: We don't change who we are as a political party just for the campaign, you know.
quotes.context: RNZ interview on Thursday morning, standing by Green candidates' attendance at a Mongrel Mob election hui after Hipkins ruled Greens and Te Pāti Māori MPs out of police and corrections portfolios.

quotes.text: Instead of investing in our public service, and the people who bring their skills, talent and dedication to the sector, the National Party is proposing cutting another 8,700 more roles and replacing them with AI.
quotes.context: Announcing the Greens' pledge to reverse National's $2.4b public service cuts at a cost of $3.17b over four years.

quotes.text: We have no shortage of talent, creativity and hard work in this beautiful country, whether it's in a South Auckland garage or a lab in Otago. What's missing is the masterplan to turn it into good jobs, higher wages and a fairer economy.
quotes.context: Launching the Greens' nearly $6b economic development plan, which the party says would create 284,000 jobs over four years.

quotes.text: Essential services like healthcare, education, and infrastructure could be funded if the super-rich and mega-corporates like the supermarkets duopoly, banks, and power companies contribute fairly to the society they profit from.
quotes.context: Greens' tax package launch.

quotes.text: The cost of food, of energy, of rent keeps climbing, while wages stay flat. Communities that were already struggling are being hit hardest by rising price, by wars they did not start...
quotes.context: Same address.

quotes.text: We believe in building an international rules-based order that protects the environment, upholds human rights and supports enduring peace-building work.
quotes.context: Same address, on foreign policy.

people.name: Chlöe Swarbrick
people.role: Green Party co-leader
people.seat: MP for Auckland Central (since 2020); contesting Auckland Central
people.background: Entered Parliament in 2017 as a list MP, won Auckland Central in 2020, and became co-leader in March 2024.
positions: Wealth, inheritance and corporate taxes, with income-tax cuts for most people.
Electrify 'everything we can'. Will work with Labour to form a government.

quotes.text: We now have a situation where a government made active decisions to knowingly potentially disenfranchise up to 400,000 New Zealanders from exercising their democratic right to vote.
quotes.context: Speaking to reporters about the government's removal of same-day enrolment, as the 25 October enrolment deadline nears (RNZ). The 400,000 figure is her claim.

quotes.text: Imagine being required to spend 30 hours a week working and not being paid for it. That's messed up. It doesn't have to be that way. The Greens will fix it.
quotes.context: On unpaid placements for trainee nurses, teachers and social workers, launching the Greens' paid placements policy.

quotes.text: We can afford to ensure that everybody retires with dignity, and that means that we have to fix the tax system.
quotes.context: Responding to National's fiscal plan and superannuation stance (reported by RNZ)

quotes.text: This is not so much a cost of living crisis as it is a cost of greed crisis, and the Greens are ready, willing and able to take on corporate vested interests.
quotes.context: Same Multi-Party Debate exchange.

quotes.text: We will ensure Government investment and incentives drive us where we all want to go: higher wages, sustained research and innovation, better education, resilient infrastructure, healthy nature and a country we can be proud of.
quotes.context: Same Greens economic development plan announcement.

quotes.text: The polls are going to continue to bounce around at the margins over the next few weeks, and this is why it's really important to understand that nothing is set in stone.
quotes.context: Reacting to a 1News–Verian poll with the Greens on 16%; she said the Greens would "very clearly" work with Labour.

quotes.text: People aren't dumb. They know that while their cost of living has gone through the roof, corporate profits have skyrocketed and the wealthiest 150 rich listers now own more than half of the country.
quotes.context: Launching the Greens' tax package (wealth, inheritance and corporate taxes; income-tax cuts for 96%).

quotes.text: No-one is hoarding, attacking, or starting wars over sun, wind, water and geothermal energy. They don't come through the Strait of Hormuz.
quotes.context: Same address.

people.name: Teanau Tuiono
people.role: Senior MP (list rank 3)
people.seat: List MP; contesting Palmerston North
people.background: List MP since 2020, of Māori and Cook Islands descent.
positions: Get 'big money out of politics' ($30k donation cap, no corporate donations).
Against 'militarisation of the Pacific'. Union membership as the default for new employees.

quotes.text: We need to get big money out of politics. The donation should only be by people, not by company.
quotes.context: Pacific Media Network interview on the Greens' $30,000 donation-cap policy.

quotes.text: Here we have the US trying to find a way to get into the Cook Islands, but is this heading towards a military base? That would be something that I would not be in favour of.
quotes.context: Same interview, on Pacific security.

quotes.text: We don't need more militarisation of the Pacific, for the Pacific to become a more contested space.
quotes.context: Same interview.

quotes.text: Individuals will still have the right to opt out if they choose to. The only difference is that workers would be opting out rather than opting in. The default should be that workers are represented and backed, not the other way around.
quotes.context: Green release on his member's bill to make union membership the default for new employees.

people.name: Tamatha Paul
people.role: Housing spokesperson; list rank 4
people.seat: MP for Wellington Central (since 2023); contesting the new Wellington North electorate
people.background: Former Wellington city councillor. Won Wellington Central in 2023.
positions: Opposed move-on orders. Says homelessness is at historic levels.

quotes.text: The most expensive road ever built in 26 years is for two kilometres of road and adds one car lane in each direction and six to eight traffic lights.
quotes.context: Aro Valley candidates' debate (Wellington North, Thursday evening), on the planned State Highway 1 upgrade in Wellington.

quotes.text: I'm not saying they should not exist altogether.
quotes.context: After saying being a billionaire was immoral (paraphrased in the same report); arguing extreme wealth should pay a fair share of tax. Date is the Midday Report interview day.

quotes.text: This is the worst homelessness in our history, with 57,000 women homeless and half of all homeless people under the age of 24. The Government's response has been a drop in the bucket to meaningfully address this crisis.
quotes.context: Green release as housing spokesperson.

quotes.text: If they comply and go home, they're not going to be charged. The minister realises they don't have a home, right? Where exactly are they supposed to move on? Should they go to your house?
quotes.context: First-reading debate on the move-on orders bill.

quotes.text: Where exactly are these kids meant to go? Would you like them to go sleep in a bush? Would you like them to go sleep under a bridge?
quotes.context: Same debate, objecting that the orders (as introduced) applied to people as young as 14. The final law applies to those 18 and over.

people.name: Julie Anne Genter
people.role: Transport spokesperson; list rank 5
people.seat: MP for Rongotai (since 2023); contesting the new Wellington Bays electorate
people.background: List MP from 2011 and a former Associate Transport Minister (2017–20). Won Rongotai in 2023.
positions: Restore intercity passenger rail ($4b). Free public transport for children and students, and a $2 adult fare.

quotes.text: Years of underinvestment in public transport have left our cities harder to get around without a car.
quotes.context: Announcing free public transport for children, students and others and a $2 adult fare.

quotes.text: Restoring commuter rail will give smaller regions and towns the benefits of more travellers stopping at their town stations, creating more economic opportunities and connecting them to main centres and other towns.
quotes.context: Announcing the Greens' $4b intercity passenger-rail plan as transport spokesperson.

quotes.text: The train journey from Auckland to Wellington is long, which makes it perfect for an overnight service. All that is needed is new, comfortable sleeper trains and operating funding.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: Neither Labour nor National is being serious or responsible about how we pay for transport.
quotes.context: Green release responding to the Government's decision to cancel next year's fuel excise increase. The Greens say the increase should go ahead and be spent on alternatives to driving.

quotes.text: We do not think a freeze is a good idea, but nor should the extra revenue go into expensive new highways. It should go into frequent bus services, passenger rail, and streets that are safe to walk and cycle on.
quotes.context: Same release.

people.name: Lan Pham
people.role: Environment spokesperson; list rank 6
people.seat: List MP (since 2023); standing list-only in Kenepuru
people.background: Ecologist. Environment Canterbury regional councillor for six years. List MP since 2023.
positions: Opposes mining on conservation land. Strongly opposes the RMA replacement laws.

quotes.text: With the passing of these bills, Aotearoa is in a new era of environmental exploitation at the hands of polluting industries.
quotes.context: Green release after the Planning Bill and Natural Environment Bill (RMA replacement) passed

quotes.text: New Zealanders expect and deserve their laws to protect and restore the environment. Instead, the Luxon Government has chosen to act on industry demands and embed climate denialism and environmental destruction into planning and environmental law.
quotes.context: Same release

quotes.text: on November 7, the Government will understand that nature may not have a voice, but voters certainly do.
quotes.context: Same release

quotes.text: Conservation land belongs to all of us. It is set aside to protect native plants, wildlife and the places New Zealanders love, not to be dug up for private profit.
quotes.context: Green release on a bill to ban new mining on public conservation land

quotes.text: New Zealanders do not want mining companies let loose on our national parks and reserves. They expect conservation land to actually be conserved.
quotes.context: Same release

people.name: David Seymour
people.role: Leader of ACT; Deputy Prime Minister (since 31 May 2025); Minister for Regulation
people.seat: MP for Epsom (since 2014); contesting Epsom
people.background: ACT leader since 2014 and the sponsor of the End of Life Choice Act. Led the Treaty Principles Bill (defeated in 2025) and the Regulatory Standards Act (passed November 2025).
positions: Wind up the Waitangi Tribunal once settlements are finished.
Welfare obligations, including drug testing. Says 'both votes belong to the voter' on vote-splitting.

quotes.text: it's essential we don't have a change of government at this time and it's also essential, in my view, that the new coalition has more ACT in it so we can actually grapple with these challenges
quotes.context: RNZ First Up interview; he said ACT's job was to ensure the coalition is re-elected (RNZ live blog).

quotes.text: The pension is linked to the wages. The only way we can help pensions in the real world is to raise wages through a stronger economy, get inflation under control, so things cost you less.
quotes.context: Answering a pensioner's question about support for disabled pensioners at the Warkworth Kōwhai Festival (RNZ live blog).

quotes.text: It's like two bald men fighting over a comb in the middle there.
quotes.context: ASB finance debate in Queenstown, 14 Oct evening, as reported by RNZ. On the clash between Willis and Edmonds over Investment Boost.

quotes.text: But the reason we need an ACT party is to take these hard positions when nobody else will.
quotes.context: On National not setting a date to raise the superannuation age (ACT would lift it three months a year to 67 by 2035)

quotes.text: You don't get higher wages from the government passing a law. You get it from risk taking and investment and innovation, people upskilling so they can produce more and get paid more.
quotes.context: Multi-Party Debate, defending ACT's preference to freeze the minimum wage.

quotes.text: If you're on a benefit you have an obligation to those paying taxes to fund it. You must be work ready, like they are. Many New Zealanders face random drug testing as a condition of work, so should the beneficiaries they fund.
quotes.context: X post backing drug testing of beneficiaries after National's welfare policy release.

quotes.text: Labour's promise to forgive 10 per cent of student loan debt will sound attractive to loan holders at first, but it is an accounting switch that should be attractive to nobody.
quotes.context: X post responding to Labour's campaign-launch student-loan policy.

quotes.text: ACT will finish the settlements and wind up the Waitangi Tribunal. The Waitangi Tribunal has been part of New Zealand's constitutional landscape for more than fifty years. It has made an important contribution, particularly in helping address historical grievances.
quotes.context: X post announcing ACT's policy to dissolve the Tribunal once historical claims are settled (post continues).

people.name: Nicole McKee
people.role: Deputy Leader of ACT (since June 2026); Minister for Courts; Associate Justice (firearms)
people.seat: List MP (since 2020); contesting Wellington Bays
people.background: Former firearms-safety instructor and spokesperson for the Council of Licensed Firearms Owners. Rewriting the Arms Act.
positions: Three Strikes for burglary, which she says needs no consultation with coalition partners first.

quotes.text: Te Pāti Māori say they want to restore their mana. They have none. They lost it when they chose a life where their profits come from the misery of others.
quotes.context: ACT press release responding to Oriini Kaipara's comments about restoring mana to Mongrel Mob members.

quotes.text: Judges keep using their leeway to give burglars more chances, and the burglars keep reoffending.
quotes.context: Announcing ACT's policy to add burglary to a Three Strikes regime (minimum three years' prison on a third strike).

quotes.text: Imprisoning repeat burglars will protect New Zealanders from a small group of offenders who have shown, time after time, that they have no respect for other people's homes or property. They will not be able to victimise us from a jail cell.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: When someone does the right thing, gets up and goes to work to unlock their own potential, they shouldn't have to worry about some deadbeat invading their home and taking their hard-earned property.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: It's a campaign election policy but I would feel that our coalition would get in behind this because they have gotten behind ACT's ideas throughout this term of government.
quotes.context: Saying there was "no need" to consult coalition partners first.

people.name: Andrew Hoggard
people.role: Minister for Biosecurity; Minister for Food Safety; Associate Agriculture
people.seat: List MP (since 2023); contesting Rangitīkei
people.background: Dairy farmer and former national president of Federated Farmers.
positions: Rural Workforce Visa. A 'science-based' split-gas approach to farm emissions.
reversals: The coalition (via the ACT agreement) promised to reverse the live-animal-export ban. In March 2026 Hoggard said Cabinet had 'not agreed any final decisions', and exporters called this a backtrack.

quotes.text: Illegal dumping is vandalism by another name. It's unfair on ratepayers, damaging to the environment, and shows a complete disregard for people who take pride in their communities.
quotes.context: ACT press release announcing higher fines for illegal rubbish dumping (as Rural Communities spokesperson).

quotes.text: Farmers deserve a massive thank you. While politicians in Wellington talk about prosperity, rural New Zealand goes out and earns it.
quotes.context: ACT release on record forecast primary-sector exports ($64.3b).

quotes.text: Punishing them with ideological targets while overseas competitors produce food less efficiently is bad for farmers, bad for consumers, and bad for the climate.
quotes.context: Same release, on ACT's 'science-based' (split-gas) climate approach for agriculture.

quotes.text: New Zealand's farms, orchards, and fishing fleets generate $60 billion in exports every year. Right now, they can't find enough capable workers to do the job, held back by a chronic labour shortage that the current immigration system simply isn't equipped to solve.
quotes.context: Announcing ACT's Rural Workforce Visa at Fieldays.

quotes.text: While discussions are ongoing, Cabinet has not agreed any final decisions.
quotes.context: On the coalition's stalled pledge to reverse the live-animal-export ban, which he said he could not get Cabinet agreement on this term.

people.name: Paul Henry
people.role: ACT candidate, list rank 4 (not an MP)
people.seat: List-only candidate
people.background: Veteran broadcaster (TVNZ Breakfast, his own TV and radio shows).
positions: Let teachers remove disruptive students and use 'reasonable force'.

quotes.text: If Chris Hipkins can’t even say no to votes for schoolkids, what hope has he got of saying no to his coalition partners?
quotes.context: ACT press release responding to Hipkins saying he was open to lowering the voting age to 16.

quotes.text: Let's be honest, there are a lot of little shits in classrooms, and we need to address that if we're going to lift education standards.
quotes.context: Announcing ACT's policy to let teachers remove disruptive students and use 'reasonable force'. Labour's education spokesperson called the language unacceptable.

quotes.text: We can't have the situation where that line is blurred. This has nothing to do with corporal punishment. This has nothing to do with punishing the child who is the problem.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: The ambiguity that exists at the moment means many teachers just can't even face the prospect of doing it.
quotes.context: Same announcement, on current guidance for physical restraint.

people.name: Karen Chhour
people.role: Minister for Children; Minister for the Prevention of Family and Sexual Violence
people.seat: List MP (since 2020); contesting North Shore
people.background: Grew up in state care, which she cites as shaping her views.
positions: A Working with Children Card. Criminalise using pets to coerce family-violence victims.

quotes.text: It is a hard slog sometimes, and it's nice to know you're not doing it alone.
quotes.context: On ACT's 'Big Pinky' campaign bus on Sunday 18 October, about candidates campaigning together (RNZ feature).

quotes.text: The Working with Children Card would give parents confidence that their children are in safe hands.
quotes.context: Announcing ACT's proposed continuous-vetting card as children's spokesperson.

quotes.text: The system ensures that cardholders are safe the whole time they work with children, not just up until a check was last completed.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

quotes.text: Nobody should have to stay in a violent home because they're worried about what will happen to their pet.
quotes.context: Announcing ACT's policy to criminalise using pets to coerce family-violence victims.

quotes.text: Family violence isn't just about physical abuse. Perpetrators use threats against beloved pets as another way to intimidate and trap their victims.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

people.name: Winston Peters
people.role: Leader of NZ First; Minister of Foreign Affairs; Racing; Rail
people.seat: List MP; list rank 1 (not contesting an electorate)
people.background: In Parliament on and off since 1978. Founded NZ First in 1993. Three times Deputy PM, most recently from November 2023 to 31 May 2025.
positions: Cut 'non-essential' immigration (20,000 resident visa cap by referendum). Abolish the Waitangi Tribunal.
Repeal the Regulatory Standards Act. Hostile to the Opportunity Party and the 'mainstream media'.
reversals: All eight NZ First MPs voted for the Regulatory Standards Act at third reading (13 November 2025). On 20 November he vowed to repeal it, saying NZ First had always opposed it but was bound by ACT's deal with National.

quotes.text: Labour’s announcement to ban social media for under 16 year olds is a naive solution to a genuine issue.
quotes.context: X post responding to Labour's online safety policy.

quotes.text: We did release our plan. Guess what it's called? It's a collective plan we got together called the Budget 2026. And there are refinements we'll give you in this election campaign, and in every case we've given you the costings.
quotes.context: Defending NZ First's decision not to release a separate fiscal plan; Labour, National and ACT have released theirs and the Greens' is due next week (RNZ live blog).

quotes.text: We've won many battles, but our mission is not complete. We've got the team, we've got the policies, and now we need you. This election, give us the tools and we will finish the job.
quotes.context: Campaign X post asking for NZ First's party vote.

quotes.text: It's a fantastic idea until you make it coercive and force it down people's throats ... If I'm getting on a train downtown and I'm in a hurry and I don't speak Māori, I'm not going to know where to go to because they decided to change all the names downtown.
quotes.context: TVNZ Multi-Party Debate, on compulsory te reo Māori and Māori station names.

quotes.text: We need to double the size of the economy and we cannot do that if we neglect the very markets we need to be in.
quotes.context: X post criticising National's plan to cut aid outside the Pacific to fund health spending.

quotes.text: The Treaty of Waitangi Tribunal has become a make-work organisation – now hearing any and all claims that in a former time would've been dismissed on application as being inappropriate.
quotes.context: X post after announcing NZ First would abolish the Waitangi Tribunal within 100 days of the next government.

quotes.text: I'm defending our democracy, and I'm proud of it.
quotes.context: Ahead of Question Time, rejecting accusations of racism over the Xu-Nan remark (which he called "drivel")

quotes.text: It was their deal, the ACT Party's deal with the National Party. We were opposed to this from the word go but you've only got so many cards you can play.
quotes.context: Vowing to repeal the Regulatory Standards Act a week after all eight NZ First MPs voted for its third reading.

people.name: Shane Jones
people.role: Deputy Leader of NZ First (since September 2025); Minister for Resources; Regional Development; Oceans and Fisheries
people.seat: List MP; contesting Northland
people.background: Former Labour MP and minister (2005–14) who joined NZ First in 2017. Champion of mining and the fast-track regime.
positions: Ministers, not expert panels, should have the final say on fast-track. Urged miners to apply before the election.
Defended Peters over the Xu-Nan remark; wants migrants to be long-term citizens before becoming politicians.
people.note: He acknowledges he is bound by Cabinet collective responsibility on fast-track, even though he 'always wanted' ministers to decide.

quotes.text: Look at my beloved fast-track, it's turned into a constipated beast.
quotes.context: ASB finance debate in Queenstown, 14 Oct evening, as reported by RNZ. Opening remarks on how slow the economy had become.

quotes.text: Now you know what our Cabinet meetings are like.
quotes.context: ASB finance debate in Queenstown, 14 Oct evening, as reported by RNZ. Interrupting a Willis–Seymour exchange on breaking up the supermarkets.

quotes.text: [Xu-Nan] should know his place.
quotes.context: Defending Peters over the Xu-Nan remark; Jones said NZ First would campaign on migrants being long-term citizens before becoming politicians

quotes.text: Providing they're not breaking the law, I feel that they should make the most of the opportunity. I don't feel that I'm being reckless.
quotes.context: As Resources Minister, urging mining companies to "get your applications in ASAP" for fast-track before the election.

quotes.text: My honest view, and I have to be bound by the collective decision, I always wanted ministers to be making the decisions.
quotes.context: Announcing NZ First would campaign on giving ministers the final say on fast-track approvals.

quotes.text: I just can't get my head around why four individuals...[are] more morally fit to make those calls than politicians and I'm going to campaign on that.
quotes.context: Same event, on expert panels deciding fast-track applications.

quotes.text: When the government was formed in 2023, the Prime Minister met with Winston and myself. I kinda got hōhā and went for a holiday to the Gold Coast so if there's anything wrong with the coalition agreement you might want to blame me.
quotes.context: Joking remark at the same event.

people.name: Casey Costello
people.role: Minister of Customs; Minister for Seniors; Associate Health (tobacco)
people.seat: List MP (since 2023); contesting Port Waikato
people.background: Former police officer and lobbyist. Elected in 2023. Health experts raised concerns about her 2026 comments on tobacco excise.
positions: Retirement village reform (rejects Labour's three-month buy-back). Says she does not intend to cut tobacco tax.

quotes.text: Seniors need more choice and more security. New Zealand First will deliver legislation that protects residents where needed, supports more housing options, and recognises the sector's role in aged care.
quotes.context: On the Retirement Villages Amendment Bill being deferred to next term.

quotes.text: Three-month buy-backs are political posturing. They would damage the sector and make residents more vulnerable.
quotes.context: Same release, rejecting Labour's policy that villages repay departing residents within three months.

quotes.text: I'm considering a review of the excise, and that's what we took forward to cabinet, that it's time that we started to consider a review on how our excise structure is for all of these products.
quotes.context: As Associate Health Minister (tobacco); health experts raised concerns, and she said she did not intend to reduce tobacco tax.

quotes.text: I want to see policies in place that stop people smoking and stop the supply of illicit cigarettes and tobacco.
quotes.context: Same interview.

people.name: Mark Patterson
people.role: Minister for Rural Communities; Associate Agriculture; Associate Regional Development
people.seat: List MP (2017–20, 2023–); contesting Taieri
people.background: Sheep and beef farmer from Otago.
positions: Regional water storage (Tukituki). Backs the Fonterra 'Use It or Lose It' policy.
people.note: He has a low media profile. Three of his quotes come from an organic-sector webinar (5 October 2026) as reported by Organic Food Together.

quotes.text: We can't necessarily live on milk powder and mutton.
quotes.context: Organics Aotearoa New Zealand 'Vote Organic' webinar (5 Oct), on food security after the McCain's and Wattie's factory closures. Reported by the organic-sector news site Organic Food Together, which links the full recording.

quotes.text: We're a biological economy.
quotes.context: Same webinar, calling cuts to bioeconomy science funding shortsighted (as reported by Organic Food Together).

quotes.text: We never quite made that line.
quotes.context: Same webinar, on the Gene Technology Bill: the coalition agreement left NZ First open to liberalising gene technology with assurances on human health and the environment (as reported by Organic Food Together).

quotes.text: National adopted most of our other policies so there's still hope.
quotes.context: Federated Farmers rural debate, asked why NZ First backs its 'Use It or Lose It' Fonterra milk-access policy when no other party does.

quotes.text: The water storage project [will] help unlock economic potential – boost food production and create jobs.
quotes.context: As Associate Regional Development Minister, announcing an $18.13m Regional Infrastructure Fund loan for the Tukituki water project.

quotes.text: As a key food-producing region, Hawke's Bay has the potential for expansion with reliable long-term water supplies.
quotes.context: Same announcement.

people.name: Alfred Ngaro
people.role: NZ First candidate, list rank 5 (not a current MP)
people.seat: Contesting Glendene
people.background: National list MP from 2011 to 2020 and a former minister. Led NewZeal, which aligned with NZ First in March 2026.
positions: Christian-conservative values. 'National sovereignty'.

quotes.text: One of the things about a bigger party is that sometimes they use this phrase, 'We're a broad church'. When you try to be all things to all people, you tend to at times compromise on the big issues.
quotes.context: 1News interview on why he chose NZ First rather than returning to National.

quotes.text: We had people giving us confidence, but not enough to get us over the threshold.
quotes.context: Same interview, on NewZeal's 2023 result; asked if the switch was pragmatism he said "realism too".

quotes.text: New Zealand First has consistently advocated for national sovereignty, the protection of democratic institutions, and policies that put New Zealanders first.
quotes.context: NewZeal release announcing he would stand for NZ First.

quotes.text: My values remain unchanged... This is not a departure from those convictions, it is an transition in how they maybe carried forward.
quotes.context: Same release (wording as published).

people.name: Rawiri Waititi
people.role: Co-leader of Te Pāti Māori
people.seat: MP for Waiariki (since 2020); contesting Waiariki
people.background: Co-leader since 2020, after winning Waiariki from Labour. Suspended from Parliament for 21 days in 2025 over the Treaty Principles Bill haka.
positions: Candidate-vote strategy aiming for an overhang. Refuses to tell voters where to put their party vote.

quotes.text: There's nothing wrong with being bilingual ... I'm quite proficient, I would say, in the English language, but the majority of Aotearoa are not proficient in my language, so they only think in one world. I think in two.
quotes.context: TVNZ Multi-Party Debate, on compulsory te reo Māori in schools.

quotes.text: You poor thing.
quotes.context: Multi-Party Debate, responding to Peters' complaint that Māori City Rail Link station names are confusing.

quotes.text: When our creativity is strong, our people are strong.
quotes.context: Te Pāti Māori press release announcing an independent Toi Māori Authority and an income programme for Māori artists, in Ōtautahi (via Scoop).
quotes.source: Te Pāti Māori release via Scoop

quotes.text: This list proves we are putting our money where our mouth is.
quotes.context: On the party's one-person list

quotes.text: You give your candidate vote to Aperehama, [and] Willow-Jean Prime - who is at seven on her party list - and Huhana Lyndon - who is also on seven on her party list - you get three... and so on and so forth, and that's how you work it out.
quotes.context: Campaign launch, explaining the candidate-vote strategy using Te Tai Tokerau as an example

quotes.text: suggestion is not ours to make
quotes.context: Asked by media which party Māori voters should give their party vote to

quotes.text: I can hear the anger and feel the pain.
quotes.context: Responding at Waitangi pōwhiri to Eru Kapa-Kingi's criticism of the party's expulsion of his mother (date shown is publication date of the report)

quotes.text: If I have done you wrong, I offer you my head.
quotes.context: Same Waitangi pōwhiri, offering an apology and suggesting another meeting with Ngāpuhi (date shown is publication date of the report)

people.name: Debbie Ngarewa-Packer
people.role: Co-leader of Te Pāti Māori
people.seat: MP for Te Tai Hauāuru (since 2023); contesting Te Tai Hauāuru
people.background: Co-leader since 2020 (list MP 2020–23). Chief executive of Ngāti Ruanui. A long-time opponent of Taranaki seabed mining.
positions: Ban seabed mining permanently. 'One plan, two votes', focused on candidate votes.

quotes.text: We said this election is bigger than any one party. Our list reflects that commitment.
quotes.context: On the party's one-person list

quotes.text: There's one plan, two votes; our plan has to be to focus on the candidate votes. We trust you with the party vote we trust and we see your love for our people, for our taiao. We trust that you will choose what is right.
quotes.context: Speech at Te Pāti Māori campaign launch, Te Poho o Rāwiri Marae, Gisborne

quotes.text: You have the power to bring this government to its knees.
quotes.context: Campaign launch speech, Gisborne

quotes.text: It's our whānau on the ground. It's not the corporate exploiters, it's not the Federated Farmers, it's not the Fonterras, it's not the BPs, it's not all the mates they're bending to - it's you.
quotes.context: Campaign launch speech, Gisborne

quotes.text: Even under fast-track legislation designed to push projects through, seabed mining has been found to cause unacceptable harm to the environment, to taonga species, and to tikanga Māori.
quotes.context: Press release reintroducing her member's bill to ban seabed mining, after the fast-track panel rejected Trans-Tasman Resources' application
quotes.source: Te Pāti Māori release via Scoop

quotes.text: Protecting our moana and standing with coastal iwi and hapū is why I got into politics in the first place. This Bill is about finishing what we started and making sure these protections are finally locked in for future generations.
quotes.context: Same seabed-mining release
quotes.source: Te Pāti Māori release via Scoop

people.name: Hana-Rāwhiti Maipi-Clarke
people.role: MP; youngest member of the 54th Parliament
